leads.name: toml_parser
leads.note: Low-level lexer and event parser without a value tree; a harness would have to assemble tables itself. Its source coverage and AFL++ feedback are recorded as the underlying parser of the selected toml and toml_edit paths (toml_parser 1.1.5+spec-1.1.0).

leads.name: basic-toml
leads.api_lead: basic_toml::from_str::<T: Deserialize>(&str); the crate exports only from_str, from_slice, to_string and Error
leads.note: No own generic value type and no datetime support: the pinned crate has no Datetime type and its tokenizer reads 1979-05-27T07:32:00Z as a number. Tried with basic_toml::from_str::<serde_json::Value> on 2026-11-17: service-config.toml fails with "invalid number at line 8 column 9" (owner.since) and typed-scalars.toml with "invalid number at line 27 column 10" (times.offset).

leads.name: toml-span

leads.license: MIT OR Apache-2.0 (LICENSE-MIT and LICENSE-APACHE in the .crate)

leads.name: nanoserde
leads.note: Tried nanoserde::TomlParser::parse(&str) on 2026-11-17 (host cargo 1.99.1): typed-scalars.toml is rejected with 'Toml error: Unexpected token Ident("0xDEAD_BEEF") , line:7 col:1' (no hexadecimal integers). Its Toml enum also has a single Num(f64) variant, so integers and floats cannot be told apart.

leads.name: facet-toml
leads.note: Found in the "toml parser" query of the recorded snapshot. Its normal dependencies at 0.46.1 are toml_parser plus the facet reflection crates (no toml or toml_edit), so it is a third tree builder over the toml_parser family already selected through toml and toml_edit. Whether a documented generic value view (facet_value) keeps the four TOML date-time kinds and int/float apart was not established; not run.
leads.round_4_decision: Checked 2026-11-18 against the 0.46.1 crate source: its only normal TOML dependency is toml_parser (a third tree builder over the toml_parser family already selected twice through toml and toml_edit), and src/parser.rs passes every date-time to facet-reflect as a plain string ("Keep as string, let facet-reflect handle datetime types"), so a generic facet value cannot tell the four date-time kinds apart without the harness re-reading the text. Not run.

leads.name: deser-toml
leads.family: deser-toml (mitsuhiko/deser; own from-scratch TOML 1.1 scanner and parser)
leads.note: Found in the "toml deserialize" query. An independent parser (src/scan.rs, parser.rs, document.rs; normal dependencies deser-core, itoa, simdutf8, zmij). Its documented API deserializes into typed deser targets; deser-core 0.10.2 has no generic value type, and date-times reach generic targets as a Datetime extension that falls back to strings, so a typed tree with the four date-time kinds needs a harness-side deser visitor that was not written in this round; not run.
leads.round_4_decision: Checked 2026-11-18 against deser-toml 0.10.2, deser 0.10.2 and deser-core 0.10.2: the crate exports only from_str/from_slice/from_reader into deser::Deserialize targets; its own document model (src/document.rs) is private, and neither deser nor deser-core ships a generic value type. A typed tree would need a harness-written Deserialize sink, which is not a documented generic value view (catalog/toml/PROTOCOL.md). Not run.

leads.name: antlr-rust-toml-parser
leads.family: antlr-rust-toml-parser (ANTLR v4 generated TOML lexer/parser with own decoder; date-time text via toml_datetime)
leads.evidence: Run in round 4 (crate sha256 f6d21f9d..., Apache-2.0): parse(&str) returns flat assignments with typed values (i64, the underscore-free float token, toml_datetime::Datetime) and [table]/[[array]] headers in source order, and its README leaves table nesting and duplicate-key semantics to the consumer. A harness that nested the items reproduced both hand-written trees, with 606 crate lines and stable AFL++ feedback (3,589 vs 3,028 edges), but placing assignments under headers and merging dotted keys and arrays of tables is harness interpretation of TOML table semantics. Under the concrete-syntax-tree rule in catalog/toml/PROTOCOL.md (a tree that leaves dotted keys and table headers unmerged does not qualify) it was demoted at integrator review; the project and overlay were removed and are reproducible from these pins.

leads.name: fig-toml
leads.family: fig-toml (diaryx-org fig language; own tokenizer and parser on fig-kit)
leads.evidence: Checked 2026-11-18 against fig 7.0.0 and fig-toml 7.0.0 sources: fig::Value keeps TOML date-times as a format-specific Ext scalar of an ExtKind (OffsetDateTime, LocalDateTime, LocalDate, LocalTime) carried verbatim as source text, and the serde path reads them as plain strings. The offset kind therefore has no decoded instant; the harness would have to parse the date-time text itself, which the TOML protocol excludes. Not run.

leads.name: flyleaf-core
leads.evidence: Its only TOML dependency is toml_edit ^0.25 (the selected toml_edit path); a document editor over toml_edit, not a parser.

leads.name: oak-toml
leads.evidence: Checked 2026-11-18: oak-toml 0.0.11 TomlValue::DateTime(String) holds the date-time as a string with no kind, so the four TOML date-time kinds cannot be told apart. Not run.

leads.name: tomlsmith
leads.evidence: Checked 2026-11-18 against the 0.4.1 source: SemanticValue::DateTime holds a DateTimeValue with only a kind, the raw source spelling and a canonical spelling (raw with T/Z and seconds normalized); no date, time or offset fields are decoded. The offset date-time UTC instant would have to be computed by parsing that source text in the harness, which the TOML protocol excludes. Integers, floats and strings are decoded. Not run.

leads.name: olpat
leads.family: taplo family (olpat is described as a maintained fork of taplo)
leads.evidence: olpat-cli describes the olpat toolkit as "a maintained fork of taplo"; the 0.14.0 crate has taplo's dependency set (logos, rowan, ahash, time). Excluded as a fork of the selected taplo path.

leads.name: babbel_toml
leads.family: babbel_toml (clockworkengineer babbel; own lexer and parser)
leads.evidence: Checked 2026-11-18 against the 0.3.0 source: Node::Datetime(TomlDatetime { kind, raw }) keeps only the kind and the raw source text; no date, time or offset fields are decoded, so the offset UTC instant would need harness-side parsing of the source text. Not run.
